result.killer: No single killer. The partial substitutes are the free TTConnect/Companies Registry filing route, general accounting and corporate-secretarial firms (Andersen TT annual returns service, Grant Thornton ORBIT), and donor-funded CSO compliance support (Cropper Foundation IGNITE CSOs). The RGD's postponement of the suspension (new date not found) weakens urgency.
result.reason: Nothing kills it outright. I found no dedicated software or packaged NPO Form 6 service, and the duty is real: about 3,000+ NPOs were flagged in the RGD notice of 26 Mar 2026. The case is still weak. Filing is free on the state route (TTConnect / Companies Registry). General firms already sell annual-return filing: Andersen TT lists "Business Registration & Annual Returns", and Grant Thornton offers corporate secretarial services. The donor-funded Cropper Foundation IGNITE CSOs project already helps NPOs with compliance, partnering with FIUTT and the NGO Unit. The suspension/cancellation exercise was postponed with no new date found, so the enforcement pressure has eased. Buyers are mostly volunteer-run clubs and churches with little ability to pay. I could not confirm the size of the register or the Form 6 fee.

result.killer: No single killer was found. The strongest blows are the IRD FAQ exemption for hotels subject to Hotel Accommodation Tax, which shrinks the Tobago guest-house and villa segment, and the very simple calculation.
result.reason:
Nothing kills this outright. I found no local LBS software, and the IRD itself says it has no official calculator. The duty applies to every landlord, quarterly, with a 5% late charge and 15% interest. But the case is weak:
(1) The tax is one rate times gross quarterly rent, so the software adds little.
(2) The IRD FAQ exempts hotels liable to Hotel Accommodation Tax. That likely removes the registered Tobago guest houses and villas the claim targets.
(3) Registration was in person at IRD offices and closed 30 June 2026, so the rush is over.
(4) Finance Bill 2026 changed the fee to one per landlord, made LBS creditable against income tax, and moves due dates to 31 Mar, 30 Jun, 30 Sep and 31 Dec. Before that the dates were 30 Apr, 31 Jul, 31 Oct and 31 Jan. Accountants already do landlords' annual returns, and they can absorb this.
How to pay online is still unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Web searches returned no T&T-specific page (only foreign results), but the OSH Act text (Chap. 88:08, unofficial LRO version updated to 31 Dec 2015, fetched as PDF from finance.gov.tt) contains the duty: every hoist or lift must be thoroughly examined every 12 months by a competent person; steam boilers, economisers and superheaters every 12 months and after major repairs, and new or second-hand ones must be examined, hydraulically tested and certified before use; air pressure containers cleaned, examined and hydraulically tested every 12 months. Each report must be entered in or attached to the General Register. The Boilers Regulations (GN 2-1949) and Air Pressure Containers Regulations (GN 3-1949) stay in force under s.98(2). The buyer is any workplace occupier with a lift, boiler or compressor; the duty is annual, with a paper register and no central portal seen. Unverified: current text (the 2015 version is unofficial and the 2004/2006 OSH Act commencement may have changed it), approved-inspector lists, and whether OSHA enforces the periodic certificate in practice. No local software competitor found in the searches, but no local-language competitor search was run.

Private water trucks: a Trinidad Express report (2023) quotes WASA's chairman saying buying water from private trucks is illegal and that suppliers use a delivery-fee loophole; WASA says it needs legislative support to act. WASA's own truck-borne water is free and may not be resold. WASA has a form for high-volume users such as car washes (WTC2022-004). No bottled-water or small-system rule found either (Food and Drugs Act is the only general hook). Nothing recurring and mandatory for a defined group; no candidate beyond a weak watch item.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Cocoa and Coffee Industry Act and Regulations (Chap. 64:20, unofficial text updated to 31 Dec 2013, fetched from FAOLEX): growers must register with the Board; buying agents need a Board licence and a TT$750 bond and must keep purchase books and submit monthly purchase and sales returns (Forms 10-13b) by the 15th of the following month; exporters need a licence and a TT$1,000 bond and file monthly returns and an annual return by 31 October; permit holders under s.4(2)(j) file monthly returns; coffee hullers need an annual licence and a monthly return (Form 19) by the 15th. Sale of Produce Act (Chap. 63:52): dealers in licensable produce need a Magistrate's licence with a bond. The current definition lists mace, nutmegs, kola nuts, tonca beans and rubber, so it is probably irrelevant to cocoa and coffee. Rice, flour and sugar trade not found to need a trader licence. The buyer pool is small (likely dozens of agents, hullers and exporters) and the rules may have been amended since 2013. Rice, sugar and flour milling were not checked.

The only mandatory item seen is national, the BIR Landlord Business Surcharge, which also covers Tobago landlords (see candidate). Unchecked: whether the THA has since passed a tourism accommodation ordinance, and Tobago-specific food-premises or vendor permits.

result.competitor: Filing is free on the state route: TTConnect lists 'File Annual Returns' and 'Comply with the NPO Act' as e-services, and the Companies Registry takes filings in person. I found no dedicated software or packaged NPO-compliance service. Local law firms and corporate secretarial agents probably offer this ad hoc, but that is unverified.
result.duty: Non-Profit Organisations Act No. 7 of 2019, as amended in 2024-2025 (LN 236 of 2024; Miscellaneous Provisions (FATF Compliance) Act 2025). An annual Form 6 return reporting controllers, members and beneficiaries is due within 30 days of the anniversary of registration or incorporation. The penalty is suspension and then cancellation of registration, and operating an unregistered NPO is an offence carrying a fine and imprisonment. The RGD issued its notice on 26 Mar 2026 and published the defaulter list on 13 Apr. It set suspension for 28 Apr 2026 and cancellation for 28 May 2026, then postponed both; no new date found. I could not read the fee or the exact LN 236 text because the gazette PDF had no extractable text. FIUTT supervises only a subset of NPOs (17 of 504 risk questionnaires in one period), which is a separate reporting stream.
result.market: More than 3,000 NPOs were flagged as non-filers in April 2026. I found no total register count; the figure was not reached in RGD or FIUTT reports. The 4,841 FIUTT supervised entities are not NPOs. A plausible total is several thousand registered NPOs, but that is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under NPO Act No. 7 of 2019 as amended, every registered NPO must file a Form 6 annual return within 30 days of its registration or incorporation anniversary. Form 6 details controllers, members and beneficiaries. A filer that misses it risks suspension and then cancellation, and operating while unregistered is an offence. In April 2026 the RGD listed more than 3,000 defaulters, then postponed enforcement; I did not find a new date. Many groups were confused about Form 29 versus Form 6, and some filings were rejected. The only tool found is the free TTConnect/RGD portal. I found no software or packaged service, but corporate secretaries likely do this informally. The filing is once a year and the form is simple. Buyers are volunteer-run with low ability to pay, so this suits an add-on or a cheap reminder-and-prep service.

result.competitor: I found no T&T software, app or done-for-you service aimed at this surcharge. Searches only turned up generic foreign landlord apps (Landlordy, LandlordTracks, Rental Tracker) with no local tax logic. The IRD says it has no official LBS calculator and that calculators circulating online are not authorised. That shows there is demand for one, and it also adds a trust barrier. A Guardian columnist says the payment method is unclear and asks whether online payment will come. None of the IRD and MoF pages I read describe e-Tax filing for the surcharge, so filing may be at BIR offices or banks. I did not confirm this. The main substitute is an accountant. The core sum is trivial (one rate on gross rent), so the software adds little.
result.duty: Real and in force. The Landlord Business Surcharge was created by the Finance Act 2025 under the Miscellaneous Taxes Act and has applied since 1 Jan 2026 (per the PwC tax summary). The IRD FAQ sets out the rules. All landlords and rent-collecting agents must register, whether resident or not. Registration costs a one-time TT$2,500 and has to be completed in person at one of four BIR offices: Port of Spain, San Fernando, Tunapuna or Scarborough (Tobago). The surcharge is paid quarterly on gross rent. It is 2.5% when quarterly rent is up to TT$20,000. Above that, 3.5% applies to all the rent, not just the excess (IRD public notice). The IRD gives due dates of 31 Mar, 30 Jun, 30 Sep and 31 Dec. Search snippets of the PwC Q2 2026 alert, whose PDF I could not open, suggest the current law has different dates (Q2 due 31 July) and that Finance Bill 2026, still awaiting assent, would move them to the dates above. So the exact dates are uncertain. Late registration costs TT$1,000 per six months for individuals and TT$2,500 for companies. Late payment adds 5% plus 15% a year interest. Changes must be reported within 30 days. Registration deadlines moved from 31 Mar to 30 May to 30 Jun 2026, and an MoF notice dated 18 Aug 2026 says registration is still open. Exempt: the State, state enterprises, hotels liable to Hotel Accommodation Tax, and public charitable, church and educational bodies. Tobago villas and guest houses registered for HAT therefore appear exempt, which weakens the Tobago angle of the claim.
result.market: Not reached. No source gave the number of landlords registered, and the Minister said early on that he had no exact figures. Reports of long queues at BIR offices suggest many thousands of individual landlords, but I found no registry count or census figure on rental dwellings.
result.reason: The duty is real, recurring each quarter and carries penalties, and I found no local tool for it. But the task is simple: one rate applied to gross rent each quarter. Registration needs an office visit and the one-off rush is over, although registration is still open. Payment appears to happen at BIR or outside software (unconfirmed), so automation has little to do. Hotels under HAT, which likely include many Tobago villas and guest houses, are exempt. Small landlords are scattered, sensitive to cost and wary of unofficial calculators. A rent ledger with surcharge reminders and receipt records, sold through property agents, is possible but would earn little. Due dates may change under Finance Bill 2026.

result.reason: The Real Estate Agents Act 2020 (Act 12 of 2020) exists. It requires registration valid 3 years, renewable, with notice of changes to the Registrar General, and makes trading unregistered an offence. Commencement is by Presidential proclamation. I found no proclamation notice. A Guardian TT article dated 6 Aug 2023 says it "awaits proclamation", and the agents' association was still waiting on Registrar General licensing criteria. So the duty is probably not in force, and the registration regime and register do not appear to be operating. FIUTT registration and AML duties are separate, in force under the Proceeds of Crime Act, and already covered as K02. Competitor search was not run beyond this. Market size was not found. Score is low because there is no live mandate, and the one running duty is K02.

LN 700 of 2026 (fetched) proclaims only s.76 and Schedule 6 (as applied to s.76) of the Gambling (Gaming and Betting) Act 2021 from 15 Sep 2026. I could not find the text of s.76, so the claim that it is a notification duty for ex-Liquor Licences Act clubs is unconfirmed. A third-party site (gamblingmaps.org) says the licensing sections are not yet proclaimed, so the licensing and fee duty looks not in force. Frequency and penalty were not found. Competitor search was not run beyond general queries; no product was found. The market is tiny (about 85 premises, per the claim's 2025 article, which I did not open), and the duty is largely one-off with a bespoke regulator process. Weak recurring SaaS case.

TTPS licensing exists (ttconnect: needs a list of intended staff, training proof "if available", background checks), but the page gives no fees, renewal cycle or penalties, so no recurring duty is documented. The Private Security Industry Bill (2019, 2022, and on the 2026 agenda) would create a Private Security Service Authority. I found no evidence it has passed, been tabled in 2026, or contains guard-register duties. Market: about 50,000 guards and "hundreds" of firms (unsourced letter and Senate motion), with no official firm count. No competing software found, but only one general competitor search was run. The duty is speculative, so the score stays low.

CDAP is real and pharmacies self-source IT to Ministry specifications (TT$68,000 fee removed). But the claims system is a state-procured computerised system run with NIPDEC and the Pharmacy Board, and I found no spec, vendor or open claim format. Pharmacies likely must use the state-mandated platform, so third-party software has no clear integration point. There is no penalty or recurring statutory filing, and the buyer pool is small (about 250-290 pharmacies). Competition and free-tool status could not be confirmed. Searches covered English only, with no deeper checks.

Duty is real: Petroleum Act Ch. 62:01 and Petroleum Regulations require a Retail Marketing Licence. The Ministry's renewal page sets a fee scale by prior-year sales (TT$1,000 for stations under 1m litres). The inspection checklist is used at renewal. A 2016 Guardian report says licences last one year, and I could not confirm the current term. No local software was found, only generic inspection apps (Fulcrum). The market is tiny: about 115-138 stations, and many are NP or Unipet-affiliated, with wholesalers handling compliance. Renewal is annual and involves a few documents, so pain and willingness to pay are low. Fine as a niche service, not a scalable SaaS. I did not verify the TTBS 6-month pump verification and did not open the renewal page.

Duty is real: the 2024 Companies Act amendments require companies to keep a beneficial owner register (10% threshold), verify it, and file annual returns. PwC reports a fine of TT$10,000 and imprisonment for non-compliance. The amnesty ran to 31 Jan 2025, and about 63,000 companies were removed. I found no 2026 deadline or strike-off exercise. I found no dedicated software product, but only two searches ran (not the planned six), so competition is not fully checked. Accountants and law firms already serve this, and the filing is episodic, so recurring pain is weak. The register is kept internally, so there is little to automate. The TTSEC regime applies only to listed entities. Market size is not quantified; the Registrar's reported 60,373 annual-return defaulters is the only figure. Low frequency and a generic-compliance feel keep the score low.
